Package dev.px.core.service

Interface Service

All Superinterfaces:
Named
All Known Implementing Classes:
AbstractService, AccountService, CommandRegistry, ConfigService, FontService, HudService, InputService, IntegrationService, NotificationService, SocialService, ThemeService, ThreadService
public interface Service extends Named
A long-lived client subsystem with a start and a stop.

The old client had eighteen managers constructed in one hand-ordered block, with the ordering constraints written down as comments: // Settings manager before event processor, // put this after everything bc it calls on ColorManager, Module Manager, .... A service states its dependencies in dependsOn() and the container works the order out, so adding a service cannot silently break an invariant nobody remembers.

  • Method Details

    • dependsOn

      default Class<? extends Service>[] dependsOn()
      Services that must be started before this one.

      Declare what you actually read during start(), not everything you eventually touch: a dependency only needs to exist before startup, and over-declaring creates cycles that are not really there.

    • start

      void start() throws Exception
      Brings the service up. Throwing aborts startup with the service named, which is the right outcome for a broken subsystem: a half-started client is worse than one that says which piece failed.
      Throws:
      Exception

    • stop

      default void stop()
      Tears the service down. Called in reverse start order, and must not throw.
